speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
धूमायन्ते व्यपेतानि ज्वलन्ति सहितानि च ।
धृतराष्ट्रोल्मुकानीव ज्ञातयो भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
dhūmāyante vyapetāni jvalanti sahitāni ca |
dhṛtarāṣṭrolmukānīva jñātayo bharatarṣabha ||
english: Apart they smoke, together they blaze: kinsmen are like firebrands, Dhritarashtra, best of the Bharatas.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
ब्राह्मणेषु च ये शूराः स्त्रीषु ज्ञातिषु गोषु च ।
वृन्तादिव फलं पक्वं धृतराष्ट्र पतन्ति ते ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇeṣu ca ye śūrāḥ strīṣu jñātiṣu goṣu ca |
vṛntādiva phalaṃ pakvaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭra patanti te ||
english: Those who show their courage against brahmins, women, kin and cows fall, Dhritarashtra, like ripe fruit from the stalk.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
महानप्येकजो वृक्षो बलवान्सुप्रतिष्ठितः ।
प्रसह्य एव वातेन शाखा स्कन्धं विमर्दितुम् ॥
iast:
mahānapyekajo vṛkṣo balavānsupratiṣṭhitaḥ |
prasahya eva vātena śākhā skandhaṃ vimarditum ||
english: Even a great tree standing alone, strong and well rooted, can be broken, branches and trunk, by the wind's force.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अथ ये सहिता वृक्षाः सङ्घशः सुप्रतिष्ठिताः ।
ते हि शीघ्रतमान्वातान्सहन्तेऽन्योन्यसंश्रयात् ॥
iast:
atha ye sahitā vṛkṣāḥ saṅghaśaḥ supratiṣṭhitāḥ |
te hi śīghratamānvātānsahante'nyonyasaṃśrayāt ||
english: But trees that stand together in groups, well rooted, withstand even the fiercest winds by supporting one another.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
एवं मनुष्यमप्येकं गुणैरपि समन्वितम् ।
शक्यं द्विषन्तो मन्यन्ते वायुर्द्रुममिवौकजम् ॥
iast:
evaṃ manuṣyamapyekaṃ guṇairapi samanvitam |
śakyaṃ dviṣanto manyante vāyurdrumamivaukajam ||
english: So too, enemies think that a person standing alone, even endowed with virtues, can be overcome, as the wind thinks of a lone tree.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अन्योन्यसमुपष्टम्भादन्योन्यापाश्रयेण च ।
ज्ञातयः सम्प्रवर्धन्ते सरसीवोत्पलान्युत ॥
iast:
anyonyasamupaṣṭambhādanyonyāpāśrayeṇa ca |
jñātayaḥ sampravardhante sarasīvotpalānyuta ||
english: By supporting one another and relying on one another, kinsmen flourish together, like lotuses in a lake.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अवध्या ब्राह्मणा गावो स्त्रियो बालाश्च ज्ञातयः ।
येषां चान्नानि भुञ्जीत ये च स्युः शरणागताः ॥
iast:
avadhyā brāhmaṇā gāvo striyo bālāśca jñātayaḥ |
yeṣāṃ cānnāni bhuñjīta ye ca syuḥ śaraṇāgatāḥ ||
english: Not to be killed are brahmins, cows, women, children, kinsmen, those whose food one has eaten, and those who come for refuge.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न मनुष्ये गुणः कश्चिदन्यो धनवताम् अपि ।
अनातुरत्वाद्भद्रं ते मृतकल्पा हि रोगिणः ॥
iast:
na manuṣye guṇaḥ kaścidanyo dhanavatām api |
anāturatvādbhadraṃ te mṛtakalpā hi rogiṇaḥ ||
english: No other quality in a person, even the wealthy, matters like freedom from illness, bless you; the sick are as good as dead.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अव्याधिजं कटुकं शीर्ष रोगं
पापानुबन्धं परुषं तीक्ष्णमुग्रम् ।
सतां पेयं यन्न पिबन्त्यसन्तो
मन्युं महाराज पिब प्रशाम्य ॥
iast:
avyādhijaṃ kaṭukaṃ śīrṣa rogaṃ
pāpānubandhaṃ paruṣaṃ tīkṣṇamugram |
satāṃ peyaṃ yanna pibantyasanto
manyuṃ mahārāja piba praśāmya ||
english: Anger is not born of disease, yet it is bitter, a headache, bound to wrongdoing, harsh, sharp and fierce. The good drink it down; the wicked do not. Drink it down, great king, and be calm.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
रोगार्दिता न फलान्याद्रियन्ते
न वै लभन्ते विषयेषु तत्त्वम् ।
दुःखोपेता रोगिणो नित्यमेव
न बुध्यन्ते धनभोगान्न सौख्यम् ॥
iast:
rogārditā na phalānyādriyante
na vai labhante viṣayeṣu tattvam |
duḥkhopetā rogiṇo nityameva
na budhyante dhanabhogānna saukhyam ||
english: Those afflicted by disease do not care for fruits, nor find the true taste of things; always in pain, the sick know neither the enjoyment of wealth nor happiness.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पुरा ह्युक्तो नाकरोस्त्वं वचो मे
द्यूते जितां द्रौपदीं प्रेक्ष्य राजन् ।
दुर्योधनं वारयेत्यक्षवत्यां
कितवत्वं पण्डिता वर्जयन्ति ॥
iast:
purā hyukto nākarostvaṃ vaco me
dyūte jitāṃ draupadīṃ prekṣya rājan |
duryodhanaṃ vārayetyakṣavatyāṃ
kitavatvaṃ paṇḍitā varjayanti ||
english: Earlier, seeing Draupadi won at the dice game, I told you, king, 'Stop Duryodhana'; you did not follow my words. The wise avoid gambling.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न तद्बलं यन्मृदुना विरुध्यते
मिश्रो धर्मस्तरसा सेवितव्यः ।
प्रध्वंसिनी क्रूरसमाहिता श्रीर्
मृदुप्रौढा गच्छति पुत्रपौत्रान् ॥
iast:
na tadbalaṃ yanmṛdunā virudhyate
miśro dharmastarasā sevitavyaḥ |
pradhvaṃsinī krūrasamāhitā śrīr
mṛduprauḍhā gacchati putrapautrān ||
english: That is not strength which opposes gentleness; dharma mixed with force should be followed. Fortune gathered by cruelty is ruinous; fortune grown through gentleness passes on to sons and grandsons.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
धार्तराष्ट्राः पाण्डवान्पालयन्तु
पाण्डोः सुतास्तव पुत्रांश्च पान्तु ।
एकारिमित्राः कुरवो ह्येकमन्त्रा
जीवन्तु राजन्सुखिनः समृद्धाः ॥
iast:
dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ pāṇḍavānpālayantu
pāṇḍoḥ sutāstava putrāṃśca pāntu |
ekārimitrāḥ kuravo hyekamantrā
jīvantu rājansukhinaḥ samṛddhāḥ ||
english: Let Dhritarashtra's sons protect the Pandavas, and let Pandu's sons protect your sons. Let the Kurus, with one enemy and one friend and one counsel, live happy and prosperous, king.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
मेढीभूतः कौरवाणां त्वमद्य
त्वय्याधीनं कुरु कुलमाजमीढ ।
पार्थान्बालान्वनवास प्रतप्तान्
गोपायस्व स्वं यशस्तात रक्षन् ॥
iast:
meḍhībhūtaḥ kauravāṇāṃ tvamadya
tvayyādhīnaṃ kuru kulamājamīḍha |
pārthānbālānvanavāsa prataptān
gopāyasva svaṃ yaśastāta rakṣan ||
english: You are today the central post of the Kauravas; the Kuru family depends on you, descendant of Ajamidha. Protect the sons of Pritha, young and scorched by forest exile, and guard your own good name, dear one.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सन्धत्स्व त्वं कौरवान्पाण्डुपुत्रैर्
मा तेऽन्तरं रिपवः प्रार्थयन्तु ।
सत्ये स्थितास्ते नरदेव सर्वे
दुर्योधनं स्थापय त्वं नरेन्द्र ॥
iast:
sandhatsva tvaṃ kauravānpāṇḍuputrair
mā te'ntaraṃ ripavaḥ prārthayantu |
satye sthitāste naradeva sarve
duryodhanaṃ sthāpaya tvaṃ narendra ||
english: Make peace between the Kauravas and the sons of Pandu; do not let enemies look for a gap between you. They all stand in truth, god among men; restrain Duryodhana, lord of men.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सप्तदशेमान्राजेन्द्र मनुः स्वायम्भुवोऽब्रवीत् ।
वैचित्रवीर्य पुरुषानाकाशं मुष्टिभिर्घ्नतः ॥
iast:
saptadaśemānrājendra manuḥ svāyambhuvo'bravīt |
vaicitravīrya puruṣānākāśaṃ muṣṭibhirghnataḥ ||
english: Svayambhuva Manu, lord of kings, spoke of these seventeen people, son of Vichitravirya, who strike the sky with their fists,

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
तानेविन्द्रस्य हि धनुरनाम्यं नमतोऽब्रवीत् ।
अथो मरीचिनः पादाननाम्यान्नमतस्तथा ॥
iast:
tānevindrasya hi dhanuranāmyaṃ namato'bravīt |
atho marīcinaḥ pādānanāmyānnamatastathā ||
english: who try to bend Indra's bow that cannot be bent, and to bend the rays of light that cannot be bent:

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यश्चाशिष्यं शासति यश् च कुप्यते
यश्चातिवेलं भजते द्विषन्तम् ।
स्त्रियश्च योऽरक्षति भद्रमस्तु ते
यश्चायाच्यं याचति यश् च कत्थते ॥
iast:
yaścāśiṣyaṃ śāsati yaś ca kupyate
yaścātivelaṃ bhajate dviṣantam |
striyaśca yo'rakṣati bhadramastu te
yaścāyācyaṃ yācati yaś ca katthate ||
english: one who instructs the unteachable, one who gets angry, one who serves an enemy beyond measure, one who does not protect women, bless you, one who begs what should not be begged, and one who boasts;

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यश्चाभिजातः प्रकरोत्यकार्यं
यश्चाबलो बलिना नित्यवैरी ।
अश्रद्दधानाय च यो ब्रवीति
यश्चाकाम्यं कामयते नरेन्द्र ॥
iast:
yaścābhijātaḥ prakarotyakāryaṃ
yaścābalo balinā nityavairī |
aśraddadhānāya ca yo bravīti
yaścākāmyaṃ kāmayate narendra ||
english: one of good birth who does what should not be done, a weak man always at enmity with the strong, one who speaks to the faithless, and one who desires what should not be desired, lord of men;

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
वध्वा हासं श्वशुरो यश् च मन्यते
वध्वा वसन्नुत यो मानकामः ।
परक्षेत्रे निर्वपति यश्च बीजं
स्त्रियं च यः परिवदतेऽतिवेलम् ॥
iast:
vadhvā hāsaṃ śvaśuro yaś ca manyate
vadhvā vasannuta yo mānakāmaḥ |
parakṣetre nirvapati yaśca bījaṃ
striyaṃ ca yaḥ parivadate'tivelam ||
english: a father-in-law who jokes with his daughter-in-law, one who lives with his daughter-in-law and wants honour, one who sows seed in another's field, and one who speaks ill of women beyond measure;

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यश्चैव लब्ध्वा न स्मरामीत्युवाच
दत्त्वा च यः कत्थति याच्यमानः ।
यश्चासतः सान्त्वमुपासतीह
एतेऽनुयान्त्यनिलं पाशहस्ताः ॥
iast:
yaścaiva labdhvā na smarāmītyuvāca
dattvā ca yaḥ katthati yācyamānaḥ |
yaścāsataḥ sāntvamupāsatīha
ete'nuyāntyanilaṃ pāśahastāḥ ||
english: one who, having received, says 'I do not remember'; one who, having given, boasts when asked; and one who courts the wicked with flattery: these follow the wind with nooses in their hands.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यस्मिन्यथा वर्तते यो मनुष्यस्
तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तितव्यं स धर्मः ।
मायाचारो मायया वर्तितव्यः
साध्वाचारः साधुना प्रत्युदेयः ॥
iast:
yasminyathā vartate yo manuṣyas
tasmiṃstathā vartitavyaṃ sa dharmaḥ |
māyācāro māyayā vartitavyaḥ
sādhvācāraḥ sādhunā pratyudeyaḥ ||
english: As a person behaves towards someone, so should one behave towards them: that is dharma. A deceiver should be met with deceit; good conduct should be returned with goodness.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
शतायुरुक्तः पुरुषः सर्ववेदेषु वै यदा ।
नाप्नोत्यथ च तत्सर्वमायुः केनेह हेतुना ॥
iast:
śatāyuruktaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvavedeṣu vai yadā |
nāpnotyatha ca tatsarvamāyuḥ keneha hetunā ||
english: When a person is said in all the Vedas to live a hundred years, why does he not reach that whole life here?

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अतिवादोऽतिमानश्च तथात्यागो नराधिपः ।
क्रोधश्चातिविवित्सा च मित्रद्रोहश्च तानि षट् ॥
iast:
ativādo'timānaśca tathātyāgo narādhipaḥ |
krodhaścātivivitsā ca mitradrohaśca tāni ṣaṭ ||
english: Excessive speech, excessive pride, lack of generosity, anger, excessive self-seeking and betraying friends: these are the six, lord of men.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
एत एवासयस्तीक्ष्णाः कृन्तन्त्यायूंषि देहिनाम् ।
एतानि मानवान्घ्नन्ति न मृत्युर्भद्रमस्तु ते ॥
iast:
eta evāsayastīkṣṇāḥ kṛntantyāyūṃṣi dehinām |
etāni mānavānghnanti na mṛtyurbhadramastu te ||
english: These are the sharp swords that cut short the lives of embodied beings. These kill people, not death; bless you.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
विश्वस्तस्यैति यो दारान्यश्चापि गुरु तक्पगः ।
वृषली पतिर्द्विजो यश्च पानपश्चैव भारत ॥
iast:
viśvastasyaiti yo dārānyaścāpi guru takpagaḥ |
vṛṣalī patirdvijo yaśca pānapaścaiva bhārata ||
english: One who goes to the wife of a man who trusts him, one who violates his teacher's bed, a twice-born man who marries a shudra woman, and a drinker, Bharata,

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
शरणागतहा चैव सर्वे ब्रह्महणैः समाः ।
एतैः समेत्य कर्तव्यं प्रायश्चित्तमिति श्रुतिः ॥
iast:
śaraṇāgatahā caiva sarve brahmahaṇaiḥ samāḥ |
etaiḥ sametya kartavyaṃ prāyaścittamiti śrutiḥ ||
english: and one who kills a refugee: all are equal to killers of brahmins. Scripture says that having fallen in with these, one must do atonement.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
गृही वदान्योऽनपविद्ध वाक्यः
शेषान्न भोकाप्यविहिंसकश् च ।
नानर्थकृत्त्यक्तकलिः कृतज्ञः
सत्यो मृदुः स्वर्गमुपैति विद्वान् ॥
iast:
gṛhī vadānyo'napaviddha vākyaḥ
śeṣānna bhokāpyavihiṃsakaś ca |
nānarthakṛttyaktakaliḥ kṛtajñaḥ
satyo mṛduḥ svargamupaiti vidvān ||
english: The wise householder who is generous, whose word is not set aside, who eats what is left after others and does no harm, who does no mischief, has given up quarrels, is grateful, truthful and gentle, reaches heaven.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सुलभाः पुरुषा राजन्सततं प्रियवादिनः ।
अप्रियस्य तु पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः ॥
iast:
sulabhāḥ puruṣā rājansatataṃ priyavādinaḥ |
apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ ||
english: People who always speak pleasantly are easy to find, king; but rare are both the speaker and the hearer of what is unpleasant yet beneficial.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यो हि धर्मं व्यपाश्रित्य हित्वा भर्तुः प्रियाप्रिये ।
अप्रियाण्याह पथ्यानि तेन राजा सहायवान् ॥
iast:
yo hi dharmaṃ vyapāśritya hitvā bhartuḥ priyāpriye |
apriyāṇyāha pathyāni tena rājā sahāyavān ||
english: One who, relying on dharma and setting aside his master's likes and dislikes, speaks unpleasant but beneficial words: through him a king has a true ally.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
त्यजेत्कुलार्थे पुरुषं ग्रामस्यार्थे कुलं त्यजेत् ।
ग्रामं जनपदस्यार्थे आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत् ॥
iast:
tyajetkulārthe puruṣaṃ grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet |
grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet ||
english: One should give up a person for the sake of the family, a family for the sake of the village, a village for the sake of the country, and the earth for the sake of the self.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
आपदर्थं धनं रक्षेद्दारान्रक्षेद्धनैरपि ।
आत्मानं सततं रक्षेद्दारैरपि धनैरपि ॥
iast:
āpadarthaṃ dhanaṃ rakṣeddārānrakṣeddhanairapi |
ātmānaṃ satataṃ rakṣeddārairapi dhanairapi ||
english: One should guard wealth against misfortune; guard one's wife even with wealth; and always guard oneself, even with wife and wealth.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
उक्तं मया द्यूतकालेऽपि राजन्
नैवं युक्तं वचनं प्रातिपीय ।
तदौषधं पथ्यमिवातुरस्य
न रोचते तव वैचित्र वीर्य ॥
iast:
uktaṃ mayā dyūtakāle'pi rājan
naivaṃ yuktaṃ vacanaṃ prātipīya |
tadauṣadhaṃ pathyamivāturasya
na rocate tava vaicitra vīrya ||
english: I said at the time of the dice game, king, that this was not right. But like medicine to a sick man, that beneficial advice did not please you, son of Vichitravirya.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
काकैरिमांश्चित्रबर्हान्मयूरान्
पराजैष्ठाः पाण्डवान्धार्तराष्ट्रैः ।
हित्वा सिंहान्क्रोष्टु कान्गूहमानः
प्राप्ते काले शोचिता त्वं नरेन्द्र ॥
iast:
kākairimāṃścitrabarhānmayūrān
parājaiṣṭhāḥ pāṇḍavāndhārtarāṣṭraiḥ |
hitvā siṃhānkroṣṭu kāngūhamānaḥ
prāpte kāle śocitā tvaṃ narendra ||
english: You have defeated these bright-plumed peacocks, the Pandavas, with crows, Dhritarashtra's sons. Abandoning lions and hiding jackals, you will grieve when the time comes, lord of men.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यस्तात न क्रुध्यति सर्वकालं
भृत्यस्य भक्तस्य हिते रतस्य ।
तस्मिन्भृत्या भर्तरि विश्वसन्ति
न चैनमापत्सु परित्यजन्ति ॥
iast:
yastāta na krudhyati sarvakālaṃ
bhṛtyasya bhaktasya hite ratasya |
tasminbhṛtyā bhartari viśvasanti
na cainamāpatsu parityajanti ||
english: Dear one, servants trust a master who is never angry with a servant who is devoted and intent on his good, and they do not abandon him in hard times.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न भृत्यानां वृत्ति संरोधनेन
बाह्यं जनं सञ्जिघृक्षेदपूर्वम् ।
त्यजन्ति ह्येनमुचितावरुद्धाः
स्निग्धा ह्यमात्याः परिहीनभोगाः ॥
iast:
na bhṛtyānāṃ vṛtti saṃrodhanena
bāhyaṃ janaṃ sañjighṛkṣedapūrvam |
tyajanti hyenamucitāvaruddhāḥ
snigdhā hyamātyāḥ parihīnabhogāḥ ||
english: One should not try to win over new outsiders by cutting off the livelihood of one's servants; deprived of what is due, even affectionate ministers abandon him.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
कृत्यानि पूर्वं परिसङ्ख्याय सर्वाण्य्
आयव्ययावनुरूपां च वृत्तिम् ।
सङ्गृह्णीयादनुरूपान्सहायान्
सहायसाध्यानि हि दुष्कराणि ॥
iast:
kṛtyāni pūrvaṃ parisaṅkhyāya sarvāṇy
āyavyayāvanurūpāṃ ca vṛttim |
saṅgṛhṇīyādanurūpānsahāyān
sahāyasādhyāni hi duṣkarāṇi ||
english: Having first reckoned up all the tasks, income and expenditure, and a fitting livelihood, one should gather suitable helpers; for difficult things are achieved with helpers.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अभिप्रायं यो विदित्वा तु भर्तुः
सर्वाणि कार्याणि करोत्यतन्द्रीः ।
वक्ता हितानामनुरक्त आर्यः
शक्तिज्ञ आत्मेव हि सोऽनुकम्प्यः ॥
iast:
abhiprāyaṃ yo viditvā tu bhartuḥ
sarvāṇi kāryāṇi karotyatandrīḥ |
vaktā hitānāmanurakta āryaḥ
śaktijña ātmeva hi so'nukampyaḥ ||
english: One who, knowing his master's intention, does all tasks without weariness, speaks what is good for him, is devoted, noble and knows his own strength, deserves compassion as one's own self.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
वाक्यं तु यो नाद्रियतेऽनुशिष्टः
प्रत्याह यश्चापि नियुज्यमानः ।
प्रज्ञाभिमानी प्रतिकूलवादी
त्याज्यः स तादृक्त्वरयैव भृत्यः ॥
iast:
vākyaṃ tu yo nādriyate'nuśiṣṭaḥ
pratyāha yaścāpi niyujyamānaḥ |
prajñābhimānī pratikūlavādī
tyājyaḥ sa tādṛktvarayaiva bhṛtyaḥ ||
english: A servant who does not heed words when instructed, who answers back when assigned, who is proud of his intellect and contrary in speech, should be let go quickly.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अस्तब्धमक्लीबमदीर्घसूत्रं
सानुक्रोशं श्लक्ष्णमहार्यमन्यैः ।
अरोग जातीयमुदारवाक्यं
दूतं वदन्त्यष्ट गुणोपपन्नम् ॥
iast:
astabdhamaklībamadīrghasūtraṃ
sānukrośaṃ ślakṣṇamahāryamanyaiḥ |
aroga jātīyamudāravākyaṃ
dūtaṃ vadantyaṣṭa guṇopapannam ||
english: Not stubborn, not timid, not slow, compassionate, gentle, not to be won over by others, of healthy stock and eloquent: they call such an envoy endowed with eight qualities.
